item.title: Historical Museum at Palazzo Civico: cross-party motion in Lugano
item.description: Ten city councillors ask to evaluate a historical museum on the second floor of Palazzo Civico, which will be liberated in 2028 with the move to Cornaredo.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - A motion proposes a historical museum at Palazzo Civico - Ten municipal councillors support the request - The second floor could become available in 2028 - The East Tower of the Pse is planned for the relocation
## Key facts - Proposal → historical museum in the spaces of Palazzo Civico - First signatory → Danilo Baratti, Verdi e Indipendenti - Signatories → ten municipal councillors - Location → Palazzo Civico di Lugano - Relocation → part of the administration to Cornaredo, East Tower of the Pse - Second floor → office move scheduled for 2028 - Exhibition → Lugano Belle Époque, extended until 8 January next year - Building → neoclassical
Ten municipal councillors in Lugano are asking for the creation of a historical museum in the spaces of Palazzo Civico. The motion is cross-party and its first signatory is Danilo Baratti, of Verdi e Indipendenti. The building houses the municipal chancellery, the wedding hall, the municipal councillors’ offices and the Municipal Council chamber.
The starting point is the transfer, planned in a few years’ time, of part of the city administration to Cornaredo, in the East Tower of the Polo sportivo e degli eventi, the Pse. The motion focuses in particular on the second floor, which would be vacated by the relocation of the Municipal Administration offices planned for 2028. The parliamentary motion calls for the future of those spaces not to be left undecided.
According to the proponents, the intended use of the spaces should be discussed before any decisions are made about their use. The text points to the risk that, in the absence of preliminary consideration of a public use, the City could end up granting them to the first commercial bidder. The motion also links this risk to the need to cover the substantial rent of the East Tower.
### A decision about the building’s future
The document defines Palazzo Civico as a public building with strong symbolic value and calls for a debate to be opened on its future. The request concerns the use of some of the spaces that could become available, not the abandonment of the entire building. Lugano Deputy Mayor Roberto Badaracco has in fact stated that the building will not be decommissioned.
According to the position expressed by the deputy mayor, Palazzo Civico will remain a landmark and an institutional seat of the City. For example, sessions of the legislature will continue to be held in the building. The motion therefore forms part of the discussion on how to pair this institutional function with a public and cultural use of any spaces that may become available.
However, the administrative step is not presented as already completed. The proposal speaks of a future relocation and spaces that would be vacated; the museum is presented as an option to be considered. The discussion is thus linked to two elements: the relocation to Cornaredo and the determination of the use of the second floor. ... ## The follow-up and issues still open
For the time being, the motion opens an assessment but does not establish the launch of a museum. Roberto Badaracco said he was willing to examine the proposal further. He did, however, recall that the transfer of some of the staff currently working at Palazzo Civico has not yet been decided. This leaves it to be determined which rooms will actually be available and when, without turning the plan indicated in the motion into an already operational certainty.
The timing of the Pse also remains to be verified. The parliamentary motion links the relocation of the second-floor offices to 2028, but the deputy mayor pointed out that it is not certain that the Pse towers will already have been built in two years. The possibility of freeing up the spaces therefore depends on a transfer to Cornaredo and on the availability of the East Tower, elements that the source presents as still requiring verification.
### Archives, storage facilities and management
If the planned relocation were to take place, according to the motion the second floor would make it possible to exhibit other objects currently kept in archives and storage facilities that are not easily accessible to the public. This reference broadens the proposal beyond the works and objects already visible in the corridors. The proposed historical museum would therefore also potentially contain materials that are not currently on display, if the vacated spaces were assigned this function.
However, the question of management remains open. Badaracco warned: «A permanent museum would entail the presence of a permanent curator». The presence of a curator is one of the points to be considered in the assessment.
The follow-up indicated by the motion is therefore a debate on the future of Palazzo Civico and a closer examination of the proposal. No definitive decision on the exhibition setup is reported: on the one hand, the transfer of the staff is still uncertain; on the other, the timing of the Pse towers remains to be verified. The discussion will have to bring together the question of the building’s cultural purpose and the functions already present in the building. The next step documented by the source therefore remains an assessment, while the spaces, timing and arrangements for any potential museum are still under discussion.

## In brief - Inspections at a Saronno auto repair shop yesterday afternoon - Two non-EU citizens found working - Both without a regular contract and the required professional qualification - Seizure and suspension until safety requirements are met and authorizations are obtained
## Key facts - Location: Saronno - Activity: auto repair shop - Intervention: Local Police - Workers found: two non-EU citizens - Irregularities: employment, safety and authorizations - Outcome: seizure and suspension of the business - Reopening: safety restored and authorizations obtained
Yesterday afternoon, the Local Police intervened at an auto repair shop in Saronno, where the inspection revealed irregularities concerning employment, safety and authorizations. At the end of the checks, the officers seized the business and ordered its suspension until the required conditions were restored and the necessary authorizations obtained.
During the inspection inside the auto repair shop, two non-EU citizens were found working. The checks established that neither had a regular contractual relationship with the company. It also emerged that both lacked the required professional qualification for the work performed.
### The irregularities identified
For one of the two workers, an irregular status in the national territory was also identified, as he was found not to have a residence permit. The check therefore concerned the relationship with the company, the qualification required for the work performed and, for one of the two people, the regularity of their stay in the national territory.
During the inspection, further irregularities relating to the business were also identified. The situation included both the administrative and safety aspects, along with the need to have the required authorizations. The overall situation led the officers to order the seizure of the auto repair shop and the suspension of its operations.
The measure therefore concerns the inspected business as a whole. The suspension was ordered until the required conditions are restored and the necessary authorizations obtained, as indicated at the end of the checks carried out by the Local Police. ## The inspection involved multiple units
The operation at the auto repair shop was carried out by officers from the Administrative and Commercial Police and the Environmental Unit, with the support of Rapid Response patrols. Multiple operational components of the Local Police were therefore involved in the same inspection of the business in Saronno.
The inspection concerned several aspects. On the one hand, the workers’ presence and their status with respect to the company were verified; on the other, issues emerged relating to professional qualifications, safety, administrative matters and authorizations. The follow-up to the intervention is defined by the suspension of the auto repair shop. Reopening will be possible only after the restoration of minimum safety conditions and the acquisition of the required authorizations. These are the conditions indicated to allow operations to resume after the seizure ordered by the officers.
### Two conditions for resuming operations
The first step concerns safety. The source refers to minimum conditions to be restored for the reopening of the auto repair shop. The second concerns authorizations, which must be obtained before operations resume. The two requirements are presented together as a condition for resuming operations.
The provision keeps these aspects together. The restoration of the prescribed conditions, already mentioned in the suspension order, must be accompanied by obtaining the necessary authorizations. The text expressly links reopening to the completion of both steps.

For the next phase, the source indicates the process provided for by the measure: the suspension continues until the required conditions are restored and the authorizations are obtained.

On Saturday 3 October, Varese hosts the Gran Fondo Tre Valli Varesine UCI time trial, the first event of the cycling weekend. The course will be closed to traffic from 11: practice runs are scheduled from 11.20 to 11.50, while the race will take place from 12 to 17.30.

The start and finish are in largo Martiri della Libertà. The route continues along via Albani, via Galileo Ferraris, via Butti and viale Valganna, then enters the Valganna SS712 viaduct. After the U-turn on the viaduct, the competitors return towards viale Valganna and travel along the SS233 out of Varese towards Induno Olona. The return route runs from Induno along the SS233, then viale Valganna, via Galileo Ferraris and via Albani.
The traffic ban in largo Martiri della Libertà, which came into force at 13 yesterday, remains in effect until 24 today. From 11 to 18, the closure affects via Albani between largo Martiri della Libertà and via Ferraris, via Galileo Ferraris between viale Valganna and via Butti, all of via Butti and viale Valganna between viale Ippodromo and the SS233/SS712 roundabout.

On Sunday 4 October, it will be the turn of the 10th Gran Fondo Tre Valli Varesine, with the event running from 9 to 17. item.description: Finance Director Christian Vitta presents the 2027 budget: possible debt exceeding 3 billion and a 360-degree review of revenue.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - 2027 deficit close to 100 million francs - Possible debt exceeding 3 billion at the end of 2027 - Vitta presents his final budget - A package for the next four years is being considered
- What → the Canton’s budget for 2027 - Deficit → close to 100 million francs - Impact of the measures → approximately 237 million francs - Interviewee → Christian Vitta, director of the Department of Finance and Economics - Possible debt → over 3 billion at the end of 2027
The 2027 budget of the Canton of Ticino closes with an operating deficit close to 100 million francs. The budget shows a shortfall approaching that threshold, but political discussion focuses mainly on what will come next: the near future and the construction of a vision for the cantonal accounts.
To present the figures, Christian Vitta, State Councillor and director of the Department of Finance and Economics, was interviewed by RSI’s SEIDISERA radio programme. This is his final budget: Vitta will not stand for re-election next April.
### The framework left by the legislature
According to Vitta, during the legislature, interventions on individual budgets produced an overall impact of approximately 237 million francs. In his account, the figure is equivalent to a multi-year package spread over several years. The choice was linked to a situation described as rapidly evolving.
Meanwhile, the framework has been enriched by three fixed points identified by the director himself: the impact of initiatives concerning health insurance funds, the federal decision on EFAS and imputed rental value. Vitta stressed that these elements were not yet present at the beginning of the legislature.
This has led to the possibility of addressing a multi-year package as well, as already happened in 2016. However, the precedent is not presented as a guarantee. Vitta referred to the case of the Canton of Fribourg, where a proposal pursued along those lines was rejected by 70% of the population. In his view, the risk is having to start from scratch. Despite this, the data point towards a package covering the next four years.
The same logic applies to sectoral reforms. In principle, Vitta explained, agreement can be broad; when it comes to individual sectors, divergences, friction and divisions emerge. The example cited is the debate over a unified police force.
Regarding revenue, the director ruled out a discussion limited solely to taxation. The reasoning will have to encompass various areas and seek any room for manoeuvre. A general increase, he observed, is difficult for the population to accept, while in other Cantons the opposite course has also been seen, with taxes being reduced.
> «So the discussion will have to be conducted from every angle.»
The budget thus opens a discussion concerning the immediate deficit, possible debt exceeding three billion at the end of 2027 and the decisions that will have to follow. It contains no specific measure for cross-border workers. For those who work between Italy and the Canton of Ticino, the text does not indicate tax rates, personal amounts or an already approved change to be translated into an individual calculation. The calcolatore fiscale may be used when any concrete measures are defined. For those who work across the border, the practical significance of the news lies in distinguishing a cantonal forecast from a decision applicable to everyday life. The text discusses revenue, taxes, expenditure and debt; however, it does not indicate a measure intended for cross-border workers, nor an individual amount to be applied.
The source neither mentions nor quantifies any measure concerning a G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax rebates or withholding tax. For a cross-border worker, this delimitation is precise: the budget concerns the Canton of Ticino, but it does not allow one to say that withholdings, social security, insurance or tax relations with Italy will change.
### The actual scope of the news
| Topic | Source's indication | Practical reading | |---|---|---| | Revenue | The discussion must cover several items, not just taxes. | No across-the-board increase is indicated. | | Expenditure | Guerra calls for cuts; Durisch argues that cuts alone are not enough. | No reduction has yet been defined. | | Package | The focus is on an intervention over the next four years. | The text does not mention an approved package. | | Debt | It could exceed three billion at the end of 2027. | This is a cantonal outlook, not an individual amount. | | 2027 result | Agustoni envisages a balanced result or figures close to balance. | The outcome remains tied to the estimates and the 2026 final accounts. |
The group leaders are divided over how to interpret the deficit. Maurizio Agustoni urges people not to be impressed by the figure of -98 million: he considers the Swiss National Bank's dividends conservative and believes it is possible to close with a balanced result or close to balance, also looking at the 2026 final accounts. This is an assessment of the expected result, not an announcement of a tax change.
The other positions concern how to intervene. Government President Marina Carobbio Guscetti does not consider a tax increase taboo. Ivo Durisch considers it worth evaluating because, in his view, resolving the situation solely through cuts is impossible. Alain Bühler considers taxes the ultima ratio and calls first for corrective measures. Michele Guerra announces a minority report and proposes acting on expenditure. Matteo Quadranti calls the budget pre-election and calls for a change of pace.
For a cross-border worker, these are political positions to follow, not rules already in force. Until the measure chosen is specified, even strumento per la dichiarazione dei redditi cannot derive a new rate or a new personal amount from the budget alone.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. The text does not assign the cross-border worker a form, a deadline or a new withholding. The procedure that can be built on the basis of the source is therefore a four-step monitoring process, not an obligation that is already in force.
### Four steps for following developments
1. Separate the figure from the proposal. The starting point is the projected deficit for 2027, close to 100 million francs. It must be kept separate from the subsequent political assumptions: the text does not yet present an individual tax measure.
2. Distinguish revenue from expenditure. Every future proposal should be assessed by checking whether it concerns taxation, other areas of revenue or spending cuts. Vitta calls for a 360-degree review; Durisch, Bühler and Guerra, by contrast, point to different priorities for putting the accounts back in order.
3. Record the political deadlines already indicated. Vitta will not stand for re-election next April. The possible package has a four-year time horizon, while debt is projected through the end of 2027. These are the time references given in the text; no other operational deadlines for cross-border workers are indicated.
4. Wait for data that may change the interpretation. Agustoni refers to the 2026 final accounts and the National Bank’s cautious estimate of dividends. Before translating the projected deficit into a personal impact, it is therefore necessary to wait until the applicable measures and figures have been specified.
The source does not indicate any offices, documents to be submitted or tax procedures linked to the budget. Therefore, the concrete step today is not to attribute to the -98 million an effect that the text does not quantify. When amounts or actual measures become available, simulatore busta paga will allow you to compare a personal scenario. To verify the tax impact of the final decision, use calcolatore fiscale.

item.description: Collision between two cars on SS707 at the outskirts of Varese: the link road between Largo Flaiano and the Laghi interchange closed for hours. Two injured, yellow code.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Collision between two cars on the SS707 on the outskirts of Varese - SS707 closed for hours between Largo Flaiano and the Laghi interchange - Traffic diverted toward the city center - Two people assisted: a man aged 55 and a woman aged 67
## Key facts - What → collision between two vehicles - Road → SS707, connection to the A8 motorway - Alert → 7.02 - Closure → for hours, in both directions - Diversion → toward the city center - People assisted → 55-year-old man and 67-year-old woman - Outcome → yellow code
### The accident on the SS707 At 7.02 the alert was raised on the outskirts of Varese for an accident along the SS707, the state road connecting to the A8 motorway. The accident involved two cars and made it necessary to close the affected section to allow rescue operations, investigations, and traffic management.
The SS707 remained closed for several hours between Largo Flaiano and the Laghi interchange, with traffic halted in both directions. Law enforcement closed the section at Largo Flaiano for vehicles heading toward Milan, while the operation at the scene was still underway.
The first information came from the AREU operations center, Soreu Laghi. The accident involved two people who were assisted: a 55-year-old man and a 67-year-old woman. This was the initial account reported for the accident between the two cars.
The Traffic Police also diverted the flow of cars toward the city center, near the Laghi interchange. The measure was adopted together with the closure, so as to allow the planned activities on the state-road section. The effect on traffic was immediate: slowdowns and queues in the area providing access to the provincial capital.
The initial medical assessment indicated a yellow code for the people involved. The source reports that they sustained serious injuries, but not injuries considered severe enough to put their lives at risk. The two road references contained in the report are therefore Largo Flaiano, the closure point for vehicles heading toward Milan, and the Laghi interchange, from which traffic was diverted toward the city center. ## Traffic management
### The closed section and the diverted flow The morning's traffic management concerned the road connection with the A8 motorway. The source identifies SS707 as the state road affected by the accident and places the closure between Largo Flaiano and the Laghi interchange. The measure, which lasted several hours, affected both directions of travel; near Largo Flaiano, the section was closed to vehicles heading toward Milan.
At the interchange for the Laghi, however, the flow of cars was directed toward the city center. The State Police managed this diversion while rescue operations, accident investigations and traffic management continued. The route taken by cars was thus shifted to the access area to the provincial capital, where the source reports slowdowns and queues.
The description of the traffic situation identifies two distinct points of the operation: Largo Flaiano, where the closure for vehicles heading toward Milan was concentrated, and the Laghi interchange, used to divert traffic toward the center. The SS707 section remained at the center of the activities required after the collision.
### Operations at the scene Alongside the State Police, the Varese Fire Brigade and the Varese Local Police intervened at the scene. The Fire Brigade worked to secure the area, while the Local Police took part in managing traffic. Rescue vehicles from the Varese Red Cross also arrived.
The activities indicated in the source therefore addressed three immediate needs: securing the area, assisting the people involved and regulating traffic. The closure of the state road made it possible to carry out these operations together with the accident investigations, while the diversion directed cars toward the city center. The result described for access to Varese was a morning marked by queues and slowdowns, while the responding forces managed traffic. ## Traffic reopened
### The medical toll After hours of closure and on-site operations, the source update reports that traffic has reopened. The SS707 was therefore reopened after the difficult morning described on the outskirts of Varese, at the end of the phase during which the section between Largo Flaiano and the Laghi interchange had remained closed for hours.
For the people involved, the rescue process continued after the initial treatment provided on site. The source reports that they were transported to hospital and specifies that one of the injured people was taken into care and evacuated to the Ospedale di Circolo di Varese.
The yellow code declared for the people involved describes serious injuries, but without danger to life. In the report, this is the medical toll associated with the collision between the two cars: two people assisted, initial treatment on site and subsequent transfer to hospital.
### The latest update The documented follow-up concerns traffic: traffic was reopened after the closure that lasted for hours and after the flow was diverted toward the city center. The previous phase had involved the section between Largo Flaiano and the Laghi interchange and had caused slowdowns and queues in the access area to the provincial capital.
The operational sequence indicated by the source includes rescue operations, investigations and traffic management. First, the people received treatment on site; then transport to hospital was arranged. On the road, the closure affected the indicated segment, while the diversion had been organized at the Laghi interchange.
The final update to the news therefore combines reopened traffic and assistance to the two people involved, with one of the injured people directed to the Ospedale di Circolo di Varese. For the morning of the accident on the outskirts of Varese, these are the developments reported by the source.

item.description: Over seventy teachers from the Insubric Region participated in Mezzana in a day of theory, practical workshops and projects on sustainability.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Over 70 teachers at the Mezzana event - Theory and workshops on sustainability - Classroom projects by mid-March 2027 - Award day scheduled for May 2027
- Where → Mezzana, Centro professionale del verde - Participants → over seventy teachers - Origin → Regione Insubrica - Theme → Communicating sustainability - Deadline → mid-March 2027 - Award day → May 2027
Mezzana hosted, at the Centro professionale del verde, the cross-border training day entitled «Communicating sustainability». More than seventy teachers from preschools, special schools, primary schools and lower-secondary schools, coming from throughout the Regione Insubrica, took part. The initiative was promoted by the Comunità di lavoro through the group «Giornate Insubriche del Verde Pulito», established to carry out activities supporting environmental protection.
The program alternated between an in-depth session and a workshop component. In the first phase, qualified experts from the Divisione della scuola del Cantone Ticino and the Ente Regionale per i servizi all'agricoltura e alle foreste di Regione Lombardia, known by the acronym ERSAF, addressed the topic of sustainability. The contributions explained how to promote a culture of sustainability in the classroom and how to explain to pupils what purpose responsible forest management serves.
The Centro professionale del verde thus became a meeting point for teachers from several school levels. The day connected theoretical discussion with proposals designed to be implemented in schools, following a path that leads from the general topic of sustainability to work with pupils.
### The transition from theory to workshops
After the two theoretical sessions, the participants actively took part in a series of practical workshops. The activities were carried out by teachers and environmental educators from éducation21, Cooperativa Sociale Koinè, Cooperativa Valgrande and the Energia futuro project of SUPSI and Dipartimento del territorio del Ticino.
The workshops offered a range of concrete proposals and ideas that could be applied with school pupils. The cross-border character of the event is reflected in the teachers' origins, as they came from throughout the Regione Insubrica, and in the collaboration between organizations from the Cantone Ticino and Regione Lombardia. For general information about vivere in Svizzera, the topic is covered in a section separate from this report. ## The planned follow-up for the classes
The most practical part of the programme lies in the planned follow-up for the classes. The day is not described as an isolated event: the proposals addressed in Mezzana must become the starting point for further study and the development of an educational project in the classroom. The objective indicated by the source is therefore to transfer the topic of sustainability from the training session to schoolwork.
### From proposal to project
To read the process without adding elements that were not announced, the steps can be reordered as follows:

item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Serious accident in the afternoon on the A2 in Coldrerio - Car crashes into truck in the emergency lay-by - The 73-year-old passenger is in life-threatening condition - The 68-year-old driver sustained minor injuries

In the afternoon, on highway 2 southbound in the Coldrerio area, a car rear-ended a truck stopped at the side of the roadway, in the emergency lay-by. For reasons yet to be established, the circumstances of the rear-end collision have not been clarified. The initial information was collected by Rescue Media and then confirmed by the Cantonal Police.
The car was being driven by a 68-year-old Swiss woman residing in the canton of Zurich, who sustained minor injuries. A 73-year-old Swiss man, also residing in the canton of Zurich, was in the vehicle as a passenger. The man's injuries were serious and life-threatening.
The initial account reported by the source therefore speaks of two injured people, with different outcomes for the driver and the passenger. The time reference indicated in the report is the afternoon, while the article update is marked at 17:45.
The accident occurred along the southbound carriageway of the A2, in the Coldrerio area. The truck was stopped at the side of the roadway, in the emergency lay-by; the car rear-ended it for reasons that remain to be established. The report distinctly describes the condition of the two occupants: minor injuries for the driver and serious, life-threatening injuries for the passenger. ## Rescue operations and transfers
Officers from the Polizia cantonale arrived at the scene. The Pompieri del Mendrisiotto arrived to provide support. The operation also involved rescuers from the Servizio Autoambulanza Mendrisiotto, referred to in the source by the acronym SAM, and Rega.
After providing first aid to the driver and the passenger, the rescuers arranged two separate transfers to the hospital. The woman was transported by ambulance; the passenger, however, was flown by helicopter. Rega's presence is mentioned in connection with the transport of the passenger and the operations required for the helicopter to land.

The report does not identify a single critical point. Instead, it lists several routes: - all roads between Mendrisio and Genestrerio; - the cantonal road between Mendrisio and Chiasso; - the S. Martino fork towards Melide; - in Lugano, the main roads in the city centre.

item.title: Swiss inflation: +1% in September driven by fuel
item.description: Swiss inflation rises by 1% annually in September: fuels lead the way, with heating oil +65%, diesel +28,7% and petrol +19,9%.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Annual inflation at 1% in September - In August it was already at 0,8% - Heating oil +65%, diesel +28,7% - Gasoline +19,9%; monthly CPI stable
## Key facts - Institutional source → FSO - Annual inflation in September → 1% - Annual inflation in August → 0,8% - Monthly CPI → stable - AWP forecasts → between 0,7% and 1,2% annually; between -0,3% and +0,2% monthly
### The change measured in September
Inflation in Switzerland accelerated by 1% year on year in September. The Federal Statistical Office (FSO) reported this on Thursday, explaining that consumer prices, already up 0,8% in August, continued to rise in the month just ended.
According to the statement, the biggest boost came from the surge in fuel prices. The text links this movement to the war in the Middle East. This is the figure that sets the tone for the September reading: the general increase in prices is presented alongside the sharp rise in fuel-related items.
### Year and month tell two different stories
By contrast, the comparison with the previous month shows a flat picture. The consumer price index (CPI) remained stable because, according to federal statisticians, opposing trends largely offset each other. The monthly figure therefore does not erase the increase observed year on year, but shows that the index's overall balance did not change between August and September.
The development was in line with the forecasts of economists surveyed by the AWP agency. For September, annual inflation was expected to be between 0,7% and 1,2%; the monthly change was forecast to be between -0,3% and +0,2%. The expectations therefore concerned two different measures, which should not be conflated with the annual figure of 1%.
### Fuel contributions
Year on year, the largest contributors to the rise in prices were heating oil, at +65%, diesel, at +28,7%, and gasoline, at +19,9%. The statement lists these three items among the drivers of the month, without providing any additional prices per litre or a breakdown by consumer categories.
The source finally broaches the subject of oil prices, indicating that further increases are on the horizon, but the text does not add a figure or date to quantify them. This distinction is also essential: the observed result is 1% year on year in September, while the outlook for possible future increases remains unquantified in the statement. ### What it means for the cross-border commuter
For a cross-border commuter who uses a car, the most direct practical connection is the fuel item. The source, however, does not indicate the price per litre, the vehicle's fuel consumption, the distance travelled or the cost of a single day. It therefore does not make it possible to turn the +19,9% for petrol or the +28,7% for diesel into an individual amount.
The same criterion applies to fuel oil: the +65% is a change referring to an item that UST lists among the main annual contributors, not an overall increase applicable to every expense. Likewise, the 1% measures Swiss annual inflation; it is not a percentage to be automatically applied to every purchase or to the commuter's entire budget.
To interpret the data in one's own case, the first filter is therefore to choose the item that is truly relevant, then keep the annual and monthly horizons separate. The move from 0,8% in August to 1% in September describes an annual acceleration already indicated by UST; it does not directly measure the cost of a single refuelling.
| Item observed | Source data | Cautious interpretation | |---|---:|---| | Annual inflation in September | 1% | Overall measure on an annual basis | | Annual inflation in August | 0,8% | Reference for the previous month | | CPI compared with the previous month | stable | No overall change indicated | | Fuel oil | +65% | One of the main contributors | | Diesel | +28,7% | One of the main contributors | | Petrol | +19,9% | One of the main contributors |
The table serves to avoid confusing different levels: the 1% concerns annual inflation, while the three fuel percentages describe individual items that contributed to the increase. They must not be added together and do not replace the CPI figure.
The scope of the press release is equally clear: the text does not discuss the G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, rebates, withholding tax, INPS or double taxation. It therefore offers no indications on administrative changes to be applied to cross-border work. To organise a separate comparison of the overall cost, one can consult confrontatore del costo della vita, without attributing to the source figures it does not contain.

The most solid procedure, using only the available information, is an orderly reading of the press release. There is no need to add an estimated figure: it is necessary to understand which data is being examined.
1. Set the period. Start with September and use August as the reference, because the source compares the annual 1% with the 0,8% for the previous month. 2. Choose the time frame. Read the annual and monthly figures separately: the former is 1%, while the CPI compared with the previous month is stable. 3. Identify the item. If the calculation concerns diesel or gasoline, look at +28,7% or +19,9%, respectively; fuel oil is listed at +65% as another contributor. 4. Separate actual figures from expectations. The 1% is the figure reported for September; AWP estimates were between 0,7% and 1,2% annually and between -0,3% and +0,2% monthly. 5. Stop the estimate at the available data. Without the price per liter, consumption and distance, the source does not allow you to calculate the cost of your trip.
### The limit to respect
The headline about possible new oil price increases does not contain a figure, date or quantified forecast in the text. Therefore, it should not be turned into a new increase that has already been measured. The correct procedure is to record that passage as an indication from the article and use, for the calculation, only the explicitly reported changes.

PAMBIO-NORANCO - Three high-end cars were stolen overnight from a garage in Noranco and subsequently recovered. Three people were arrested in different locations. The operation was announced by the Public Prosecutor's Office and the Cantonal Police.
The burglary was reported shortly after 2.30 last night. According to initial findings, the perpetrators first stole the keys to three vehicles, then took the cars and fled.

item.title: Switzerland, entry tax of up to 4 thousand francs
item.description: The Swiss proposal provides for an incentive tax between 2 thousand and 4 thousand francs, linked to the safeguard clause for EU citizens.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Proposed tax: between 2,000 and 4,000 francs - It is linked to the safeguard clause - At least 4,000 for employees and self-employed workers - 2,000 for family reunification
## Key facts - Measure → incentive tax - Scope → citizens of the European Union - Condition → effective activation of the safeguard clause - Employees, self-employed workers and people without gainful activity → at least 4,000 francs - Family reunification → 2,000 francs
Between 2,000 and 4,000 Swiss francs: this is the range of the incentive tax that Switzerland aims to include in the package of bilateral agreements with the European Union. The proposal has been discussed and the legislative text remains under discussion. The issue is part of the Council of States' tightening and concerns the safeguard clause linked to the entry of EU citizens.
The reference is to those who move across the border in the categories covered by the legislative text under discussion. For cross-border readers, the scope must be kept separate from other issues: the text does not mention permit G, Canton Ticino, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax rebates, withholding tax, INPS or double taxation. It therefore provides no basis for attributing a specific change to these issues. Permesso G/B remains outside the scope described.
### The clause as a condition
The operational point is the link between the tax and the clause. The measure is not presented as an autonomous levy for every entry: it would be rigidly tied to the effective activation of the safeguard clause. The latter is described as the legal instrument that Switzerland intends to activate to limit the entry of EU citizens whenever it is assessed that immigration is causing serious social and economic problems in the country.
According to the hard line set out in Switzerland, the Swiss executive would be obliged to consider applying the clause when the entry threshold were exceeded in even just one of the four key parameters referred to in the text. Those listed include net immigration from the European Union, the level and trend of unemployment, and the rate of reliance on social assistance.
If the clause is effectively activated, the amount changes according to the category of entry. For employees, self-employed workers and people without gainful activity, the amount would be at least 4,000 francs. For salaried employees, the charge would fall directly on the company making the hire. In the case of family reunification, the amount would drop to 2,000 francs and would apply to all adult citizens who choose to reunite with family members already resident in Switzerland. ## What changes for the different categories
### The difference between entry and commuting
The proposed measure does not use a single amount. The text distinguishes the entry category and the employment or family situation; for those reading from the border area, this is the first distinction that should not be overlooked. The table rearranges the elements expressly indicated:
| Profile indicated | Amount provided | Specific element | |---|---:|---| | Subordinate employee | at least 4 thousand francs | payment borne by the hiring company | | Self-employed worker | at least 4 thousand francs | category included in the text | | Person without gainful activity | at least 4 thousand francs | category included in the text | | Adult citizen for family reunification | 2 thousand francs | family members already residing in Switzerland |
The first practical consequence is that the word worker alone is not enough to determine the applicable treatment. A subordinate employee is associated with a charge for the company carrying out the hiring; self-employed people and people without gainful activity fall into the same minimum bracket, but the proposal does not indicate a different paying party. In family reunification, by contrast, what matters is being of legal age and the presence of family members already residing in Switzerland.
There is also a distinction that must be kept clear for the cross-border commuter. The source speaks of people who move across the border and of entries by citizens of the European Union. item.title: Unemployment for cross-border workers, the rules could change
item.description: The current rules for cross-border workers residing in Italy provide for NASpI. A European revision could shift responsibility to the country of last employment after 22 consecutive weeks.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Today, the state of residence normally matters - In Italy, NASpI applies if the requirements are met - The revision indicates at least 22 consecutive weeks - Date reported by the source: 28 September 2026
## Key facts - Competent state today → State of residence - Benefit for Italian residents → NASpI - Period in the other state → at least 22 consecutive weeks - Institutions mentioned → SECO, INPS - Scope → coordination of social security systems
The source associates the date 28 September 2026 with the final approval by the Council of the European Union of the revision of the rules on the coordination of social security systems. The revision also concerns unemployment for workers who live in one state and work in another.
This point concerns cross-border workers residing in Italy who work in Switzerland and completely lose their jobs. According to the rules currently described, the relevant state is normally the state of residence: for an Italian resident, this means turning to the Italian system and potentially accessing NASpI, provided the requirements set out by the legislation are met.
### The current principle
SECO, Switzerland’s State Secretariat for Economic Affairs, indicates that so-called «true cross-border workers» receive benefits in their state of residence in the event of complete unemployment. The INPS page dedicated to unemployment among cross-border workers confirms the same approach: for those residing in Italy, the NASpI rules apply.
This criterion also applies if, during the employment period, contributions were paid in the country where the employer was located. However, the years worked in Switzerland are not ignored: insurance and contribution periods accrued in the state of last employment may be taken into account when verifying entitlement to the benefit.
The possible change stems from the new European legislation. A worker who has carried out their activity in another state for at least 22 consecutive weeks could receive, subject to the conditions laid down by national legislation, the allowance from the country of last employment rather than from the country of residence.
The revision also concerns family benefits, posted workers and those working in multiple states. For Italian cross-border workers employed in Canton Ticino, the source speaks of particularly important consequences for the thousands of workers concerned. However, the change would depend on the rule being adopted in relations between Switzerland and the European Union. The source reports that this very possible consequence prompted Swiss policymakers to take action.
For more information on the mechanism described, guida alla disoccupazione dei frontalieri can be consulted, distinguishing the current framework from the European scenario. ## The comparison for those working in Ticino
For a cross-border worker, the difference concerns not only the entity that pays the benefit. The connecting factor changes: under the current rules, residence prevails, whereas under the European revision described by the source, the country of the last activity may become decisive, provided the national conditions are met.
### Before and after
| Situation | Current rule | Scenario described by the revision | | Complete loss of work | Benefit paid in the State of residence | Benefit paid in the State of last employment | | Resident in Italy, working in Switzerland | Reference to the Italian system and NASpI | Possible reference to the Swiss system, if the rule applies to Switzerland |
The source uses a specific case to show the difference: a worker residing in Como, employed in Lugano for some time, loses their job. Under the current rules, they would normally turn to Italy; if the new European system were also applied to Switzerland, the Swiss system could instead be responsible for paying the benefit.
That proviso limits the practical effect of the news. The European revision is described as a possible change in relations with Switzerland, not as an automatic change already in force for those working in Canton Ticino. The threshold of 22 consecutive weeks should not be considered in isolation either: entitlement remains tied to the conditions of national legislation.
A cross-border worker must therefore distinguish between two questions: where they reside and where they carried out their last activity. The former currently determines which State to turn to; the latter could determine the country responsible for payment if the revision is applied. The insurance and contribution periods in the State of last employment remain relevant to establishing entitlement.
The dossier should not be confused with different topics such as a G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, rebates, withholding tax or double taxation: here the source examines the benefit in the event of complete unemployment. To follow this distinction, consult the in-depth article on disoccupazione dei frontalieri.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## How to read the specific case
The operational process starts with the correct classification of the situation, not with the place where the contributions were paid. The source makes it possible to follow a simple sequence, without confusing the rules currently indicated with the European hypothesis.
### Five checks
1. Verify that this is a case of complete unemployment. This is the situation to which the rule indicated by SECO, the reference to INPS and the possible shift toward the last employment relate. 2. Identify the State of residence. If the cross-border worker resides in Italy, the current framework normally leads to the Italian system and the NASpI rules, subject to the requirements. 3. Indicate the State of the last employment. The insurance and contribution periods accrued there may be taken into account to verify entitlement, even if the benefit is normally now the responsibility of the State of residence. 4. Check the threshold indicated by the European revision. The activity in the other State must reach at least 22 consecutive weeks, subject to the conditions of national legislation. 5. Verify the Switzerland-EU scope. The shift toward the country of the last activity is described as possible only if the new system is also applied to relations between Switzerland and the European Union.
For those living in the provinces of Como, Varese or Verbano-Cusio-Ossola and working in Canton Ticino, this sequence lines up the elements present in the source: residence, complete loss of employment, last employment and insurance or contribution periods. The conditions of national legislation remain applicable both to NASpI and to any new rule.
The date should also be reported without attributing automatic effects to it: 28 September 2026 is the date reported by the source alongside the European Union Council's final approval. The text, however, links any change for cross-border workers to its application in relations with Switzerland. To follow the evolution of the criterion and check the comparison between residence and last employment, consult guida alla disoccupazione dei frontalieri.

item.title: Traffic chaos on August 8: working group evaluates improvements
item.description: After more than four hours of chaos in the Luganese, the Cantonal Police sets up a working group on the closure of the A2 in Mezzovico-Vira and the traffic disruption.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Over four hours of disruption in the Lugano area. - The A2 was closed at Mezzovico-Vira. - The cantonal police set up a working group.
## Key facts - Date → evening of August 8 - Location → Mezzovico-Vira and the Lugano area's road network - Vehicles involved → two, completely destroyed - Injured → seven, two of them seriously - Presence in the lane → oil and fluids - Parliamentary motion → Stefano Quadri and co-signatories - Development → cantonal police working group
### The evening of August 8 On the evening of August 8, the Lugano area's road network was affected by traffic disruptions lasting more than four hours. The cantonal police set up a working group following that situation, which occurred after the closure of the A2 near Mezzovico-Vira.
The closure had been decided because of a major accident. Two vehicles were completely destroyed in the incident, including a camper van with a gas cylinder inside. Seven people were injured, two of them seriously. Oil and fluid leaks were also recorded in the lane, while assessment activities were necessary.
These factors accompanied an evening of major difficulties on the Lugano area's road network. The affair sparked controversy and a parliamentary motion submitted by Grand Council member Stefano Quadri together with the co-signatories. This institutional step led the Council of State to reconstruct what had happened, explain the reasons for the long time taken to reopen the A2, and announce the establishment of the working group.
The Government's response therefore retraces the management of the closure and the operational follow-up. The cantonal police set up the group, while the Council of State linked the announcement to the evening of August 8 and the widespread disruptions throughout the Lugano area's road network. The reconstruction includes the accident at Mezzovico-Vira, the consequences in the lane, and the activities required before reopening.
The response thus brings together the accident data and traffic management: the Council of State retraces the evening and links those disruptions to the announcement of the working group. ## Why reopening took time
### Safety and pressure on the network The explanation provided by the State Council starts with the activities that must be carried out after the major accident in Mezzovico. Rescue and survey operations must be able to take place in complete safety. For this reason, according to existing protocols, reopening to traffic is pursued as quickly as possible, but the complete closure of both lanes is almost always necessary.
The Government specified that the incident in Mezzovico occurred on a day of heavy traffic. In that situation, it explained, it was not possible to do otherwise. Several scenarios were assessed with the aim of easing pressure on the road network, but the circumstances at the time did not allow effective solutions to be adopted.
The closure of the A2 was not the only thing that made the situation more difficult to manage. Because of the high number of vehicles on the road, the cantonal road was also completely congested. The Government's response therefore describes pressure extending beyond the closure point, affecting the cantonal road network in the Luganese area.
In fact, several accidents occurred on the same cantonal road, at the roundabout providing access to the Vedeggio-Cassarate tunnel. These incidents further worsened traffic conditions. The State Council's reconstruction links the timing of the reopening and the extent of the disruption to the need to operate safely, heavy traffic, and congestion that also spread to the cantonal road.
The Cantonal Police did everything possible to limit the duration of the closures and allow traffic to pass on at least one lane, while the scenarios assessed did not prove effective under the prevailing conditions. The picture described by the Government therefore includes the rescue and survey operations, the high number of vehicles, and the additional accidents recorded along the cantonal road network. ## The follow-up: a review of operations
### From the political response to the working group The follow-up announced by the Council of State is the establishment of a working group by the cantonal police. The structure is presented as part of what takes place for every operational process and, at the same time, as a response to the management of an exceptional situation. The task indicated in the response is to verify the effectiveness of the procedures adopted and, where necessary, identify any room for improvement and make the appropriate corrections.
The announcement comes in the response to the parliamentary motion submitted by Grand Council member Stefano Quadri and the co-signatories. The Council of State used that response to retrace the events of the evening, clarify the reasons for the lengthy reopening time for the A2 and explain the operational context in which the decision to establish the group was made.
The Government summarised the operational criterion in these words:
> «in accordance with existing protocols, efforts are made to reopen the road to traffic as soon as possible, but rescue operations and surveying activities must be carried out in complete safety, and this almost always requires both lanes to be fully closed»
The statement defines the criterion referred to in the response: reopening must be pursued quickly, but without compromising the safety of operations. According to the Council of State's explanation, the cantonal police did everything possible to reduce the duration of the closures and allow passage on at least one lane. The review can therefore concern the effectiveness of the operational process and consider, if necessary, the adjustments indicated by the Government.
For the evening in Mezzovico, the next step indicated by the Government is therefore the evaluation work. The establishment of the group makes it possible to examine the exceptional situation according to the logic indicated by the Council of State: verify effectiveness, identify any room for improvement and, if necessary, make the appropriate corrections.

The political movement’s statement asks for explanations about what happened and the consequences of the train’s stoppage for rail traffic.
### Reconstruction of the incident
According to Europa Verde’s reconstruction, the train reportedly stopped about 200 metres from Busto Arsizio FS station. However, according to testimonies cited by the movement, the short distance from the platform did not result in authorization to evacuate the train and escort passengers safely to the station.
According to the statement, passengers reportedly remained inside the train for more than three hours. The source specifies that the opening photo of the original article is a file photo and does not concern this incident: a point that Europa Verde distinguishes from the reconstruction of the breakdown.
The questions are addressed to the operators of the infrastructure and rail service, identified respectively as Rfi and Trenord. Europa Verde asks why passengers were not authorized to get off and why, according to the reconstruction contained in the statement, three hours were needed to arrange for the train to be towed to Busto Arsizio station.
The movement links the case to the debate on the reliability of the cross-border connection, also discussed in Switzerland. In the statement, it argues that:
> «Switzerland is in fact beginning to consider the service operated in Italy as not up to standard and is loudly calling for the shuttle bus service to Malpensa to be reactivated, as it is considered more reliable and more punctual».
This position forms part of Europa Verde’s criticism of the quality of the rail service and the management of disruptions affecting commuters in the area. Finally, the movement asks what measures will be taken to prevent travellers from being left on the train for hours without answers. ## What emerges for those crossing the border
For the cross-border commuter who uses the S50, the episode described by Europa Verde should be viewed on two levels: the continuity of the cross-border connection and the practical management of passengers when the train stops. The source provides no schedules, frequencies, normal journey times or alternative routes; it is therefore not possible to turn this case into a general measure of the line. The practical fact documented is another: a train bound for Bellinzona reportedly stopped near a station and, according to the movement's account, the passengers reportedly remained on board for over three hours.
### Two different questions
The first issue concerns safety and evacuation. Europa Verde reports testimonies about the failure to authorize passengers to get off, not a formally reported decision in the source with reasons from the operators. The second concerns the recovery of the train: the note asks why three hours were needed to organize the towing to Busto Arsizio. Separating the two levels avoids reducing everything to a simple delay: on the one hand, there is what was reportedly communicated by the operations room; on the other, the time attributed to organizing the intervention.
| Profile | What the note reports | |---|---| | Passengers | They reportedly remained on the train for over three hours | | Evacuation | The authorization referred to in the testimonies reportedly did not arrive | | Towing | Europa Verde asks for explanations about the three hours indicated in the account | | Alternative service | The movement recalls the request to reactivate the shuttle bus to Malpensa |
For those traveling between Italy and Switzerland, the part about the shuttle bus should be considered a position contained in the statement, not the announcement of a service that has already been reactivated. Europa Verde maintains that in Switzerland the connection operated in Italian territory is considered inadequate and that the bus is regarded as more reliable and punctual. The source does not indicate which authority made a decision, nor does it provide a timetable.

item.title: A2 accident in Mendrisio: queues for cross-border commuters
item.description: Accident in Coldrerio on the A2: a 68-year-old woman slightly injured, a 73-year-old man in life-threatening condition, and delays of up to an hour and a half toward Chiasso for cross-border commuters.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Accident shortly before 15.30 in Coldrerio - 73-year-old in life-threatening condition after the rear-end collision - A2 closed between Mendrisio and Chiasso - Delays of up to an hour and a half on the Rivera-Chiasso route
## Key facts - Location: Coldrerio - Time: shortly before 15.30 - Circumstances: car collided with an articulated lorry stopped in the emergency lay-by - Injured: 68-year-old with minor injuries; 73-year-old in life-threatening condition - Closure: Mendrisio-Chiasso section - Delays: up to an hour and a half on the Rivera-Chiasso route - Roads affected: Mendrisio, Genestrerio, Balerna and Chiasso
### The sequence of the emergency
Shortly before 15.30, in Coldrerio, a car driven by a 68-year-old Swiss woman collided with an articulated lorry stopped in the emergency lay-by. The driver sustained minor injuries. The passenger, a 73-year-old man, was instead airlifted to hospital in life-threatening condition.
The accident required the intervention of emergency services and the landing of Rega. To allow these operations, the A2 was temporarily closed between Mendrisio and Chiasso. The closure therefore affected a section also used by cross-border workers from the province of Varese on their journey home from Switzerland.
The reopening of the motorway came after the phase required for the emergency response, but it did not immediately restore normal conditions. Traffic continued to suffer heavy disruption, extending the problems beyond the section directly affected by the accident.
TCS estimated delays of up to an hour and a half on the Rivera-Chiasso route. The estimate concerns the direction indicated in the report and conveys the extent of the slowdown recorded in the afternoon, without providing separate times for each individual point on the A2.
Meanwhile, traffic diverted onto ordinary roads brought Mendrisio and the roads toward Genestrerio, Balerna and Chiasso to a standstill. The problem therefore did not remain confined to the motorway: the local road network also absorbed vehicles leaving the main route.
For cross-border workers from Varese, the most delicate moment coincided with the time of the return journey to Italy. The long queues affected workers using the A2 to return from Switzerland, while the Mendrisiotto remained paralysed by the impact on traffic.
The situation therefore followed a precise progression: the accident in Coldrerio, the temporary suspension of motorway traffic between Mendrisio and Chiasso, the reopening and finally the diversion of traffic onto ordinary roads. These stages, all indicated in the reconstruction, explain why the disruption affected not only the site of the rear-end collision, but also the return journey through the Mendrisiotto. The report explicitly links these repercussions to the time when workers were returning to the province of Varese. For the cross-border commuter returning to the province of Varese, the criticality described by the source does not end at the time of closure. The decisive step is the sequence between the motorway and ordinary roads: even after the reopening of the A2, the repercussions continued to weigh on the Mendrisiotto and on the roads towards Genestrerio, Balerna and Chiasso.
### Three steps to distinguish
Reading the episode in phases helps not to confuse the reopening of the motorway with the return to normality. The source describes three distinct moments:
| Phase | Reported data | Described relapse | |---|---|---| | Rescue | A2 closed between Mendrisio and Chiasso | Motorway traffic temporarily suspended | | After reopening | A2 open again | Heavy impact on traffic | | Ordinary roads | Traffic poured onto local roads | Mendrisio and the routes towards Genestrerio, Balerna and Chiasso in a tailspin |
For the worker who has to return, the most concrete data remains the TCS estimate: up to an hour and a half on the Rivera-Chiasso section. It is an estimate referring to the indicated section, not a scan of the minutes lost in each municipality. The source does not provide separate times for reopening, nor a ranking of slowdowns between Mendrisio, Genestrerio, Balerna and Chiasso.
This limit should also be kept in mind when looking for alternative routes. Local roads are mentioned because they received traffic and were found to be in a tailspin; the news does not present them as free detours. Therefore, it is not possible to derive a guaranteed route from the source to avoid queues. For a comparison with other episodes, the site offers storico del traffico e delle code, without turning the reconstruction into a prediction.
It is a chronicle of the road system of the Canton of Ticino, not a news item on G permits, AHV, LPP, LPP, LAMal, rebates, withholding tax or double taxation. These issues are not dealt with in the source; the link for the cross-border commuter is instead the daily journey to the province of Varese and the risk of long queues at the time of return.
The useful data is therefore geographical and temporal: Coldrerio is the point of the accident, Rivera-Chiasso the section for which the delay is estimated, while Mendrisio, Genestrerio, Balerna and Chiasso are the places involved in ordinary traffic.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ### Checklist for re-entry
A cross-border commuter who is faced with similar news can read it with an operational sequence built only on the available data. It is not a diversion map, because the source does not indicate alternative routes; it serves to separate what is confirmed from what is not indicated.
1. Locate the critical point. The event took place in Coldrerio, on the A2. This identifies the stretch of the news and does not allow the conditions of the rest of the route to be established, because the source does not provide that data.
2. Distinguish between the two phases. The A2 was first closed between Mendrisio and Chiasso for rescue and landing of Rega, then reopened. The reopening, on its own, does not coincide with the end of the disruptions described.
3. Use the estimate without turning it into a promise. The TCS has indicated delays of up to an hour and a half on the Rivera-Chiasso route. It is the quantitative reference available; the source does not allocate that time to each trip, each municipality or each lane.
4. It treats the ordinary road system as an affected area, not as a guaranteed alternative. Mendrisio and the roads towards Genestrerio, Balerna and Chiasso were affected by the poured traffic. The news does not say which road was free nor does it provide a replacement route.
5. Separate the news from other practices. The episode concerns the return journey of Varese cross-border workers. To check other queue episodes, consult the tempi di attesa ai valichi and use the storico del traffico e delle code as an archive, without attributing further data to this source.
This reading allows you to organize the return on the basis of place, phase and estimate available, avoiding adding times or routes that the article does not report. The news does not contain a health, tax or social security procedure: its only practical hook is the circulation on the route also used by cross-border commuters towards the province of Varese.

item.title: AHV slightly up from January
item.description: From January, the minimum AHV/IV pension will rise to 1,280 francs, the maximum to 2,560 francs. Minimum contributions and supplementary benefits will also increase.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Minimum AHV/IV pension: 1,280 francs per month - Maximum pension: 2,560 francs with full contribution - Price and wage adjustment: 1.59% - Additional costs: approx. 7 million for the Confederation
## Key Facts - Effective → January next year - Decision → Federal Council, Friday - Minimum AHV/IV pension → CHF 1,260 to CHF 1,280 per month - Maximum pension → from 2,520 to 2,560 francs - Adjustment → the evolution of prices and wages, +1.59% - Minimum contribution for self-employed and non-gainfully employed persons (AHV, IV and EO) → CHF 530 to CHF 541 per year - Voluntary AHV/IV → CHF 1,010 to CHF 1,030 - Additional costs → around 7 million for the Confederation and 4 million for the cantons
From January next year, pension pensions will become slightly higher. On Friday, the Federal Council decided to adjust the amounts to 1.59% in line with price and wage developments.
The figure concerns the social security items indicated in the note: AHV, IV and, for some minimum contributions, IPG. For cross-border commuters working in the Canton of Ticino, the source does not distinguish between residents and people living across the border and does not indicate a specific regulation for permesso G/B.
### Pensions and contributions
| Voice | Before | From January | |---|---:|---:| | Minimum AHV/IV pension | 1,260 francs per month | 1,280 francs per month | | Maximum pension | 2,520 francs | 2,560 francs | | Minimum AHV, IV and EO contribution | CHF 530 per year | CHF 541 per year | | Voluntary AHV/IV | CHF 1,010 | CHF 1,030 |
For the maximum pension, the source specifies that the amounts indicated are paid if the contribution period is full. For an incomplete duration, however, the text does not indicate a different amount. The minimum contribution of the self-employed and non-gainfully employed persons to AHV, IV and EO is increased from CHF 530 to CHF 541 per year; that for the voluntary AHV/IV increases from CHF 1,010 to CHF 1,030.
The adjustment of pensions will lead to an overall increase in expenses of around 1,055 million francs: 940 million for the AHV, of which 190 million will be borne by the Confederation, equal to 20.2% of insurance expenditure, and 115 million for the IV, of which 44 million will be borne by the Confederation, equal to 37.7% of expenditure.
For supplementary benefits and bridging benefits, the annual amounts allocated to cover general living needs increase to 21,000 francs for single persons, compared to 20,670, and to 31,500 francs for married couples, compared to 31,005. For children, the amount is 10,980 francs if they have already reached the age of 11 and 7,710 francs if they have not yet completed them. These adjustments add about 7 million francs to be borne by the Confederation and 4 million by the cantons; the note does not allocate a specific share to the Canton of Ticino. For the cross-border commuter, the news should be read as a grid of items, not as a single increase applicable to each person. The source lumps together monthly pensions, minimum contributions and annual benefits, but assigns each amount to a different audience. The first practical question is therefore which item is being read, not how much it generically increases the pension.
### A reading by categories
The minimum AHV/IV pension is a monthly amount. The minimum contribution for the self-employed and non-gainfully employed persons, on the other hand, is expressed on an annual basis and includes AHV, IV and EO. The contribution for the voluntary AHV/IV is a separate item. For those who cross the border to work, this separation avoids putting a pension and a contribution payment on the same footing: the text does not present the minimum contribution as a general deduction valid for every employee.
The maximum pension also requires careful reading. The note links the maximum amounts to the full contribution period and does not provide an alternative figure for those who do not reach that duration. The cross-border commuter cannot therefore derive a personal amount from the information alone if his position does not coincide with the condition indicated.
Supplementary and transitional benefits follow yet another logic: the amounts are annual and change according to the category indicated, i.e. single person, married couple or child over or under 11 years of age. The source does not add any other criteria, monthly payments or administrative steps. This limit prevents the annual amounts from being converted into a monthly payment promise.
### What Stays Out of the Note
The measure concerns the AHV/IV items and the minimum contributions mentioned. However, it does not enter into BVG, KVG, withholding tax, rebates or double taxation. It does not even deal with INPS, the new 2026 tax agreement or the Brogeda pass. For the reader with a G permit, these topics cannot be updated on the basis of this source alone. Even the reference to the 4 million for the cantons does not allow a specific figure to be attributed to the Canton of Ticino.
To keep your pension provision separate from the other chapters of cross-border work, you can consult approfondimento sulla pensione AVS.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. Personal verification can be done without adding data that the note does not contain. For the cross-border commuter, the most solid method is to separate the starting date, category, unit of measurement and contribution condition. In this way, the decision is read for what it communicates, without turning it into a new tax rule or an administrative procedure.
### Five Controls
1. **Set the effective date.** The only time reference provided is from January next year. The text does not indicate a precise day of the month.
2. Identify the item. Distinguish the minimum AHV/IV pension from the maximum pension. If you are checking a contribution, check whether the description refers to self-employed and non-gainfully employed persons or the voluntary AHV/IV.
3. Check the unit of measurement. Pensions are expressed per month, while the minimum contributions and amounts for supplementary and bridging benefits are indicated on an annual basis.
4. Check the stated condition. A full contribution period is required for the maximum pension. For the amounts intended for general living needs, the source distinguishes between single persons, married couples and children who have already reached the age of 11 or have not yet turned 11.
5. Keep public costs separate. The approximately 1,055 million in additional expenditure for pension adjustments, as well as the approximately 7 million to be borne by the Confederation and the 4 million to be borne by the cantons for other adjustments, are not presented as sums to be paid individually.
This check also avoids automatically reading the note as a change to the position of each cross-border commuter. The source does not indicate forms, documents, offices or a separate procedure for the G permit and does not give workers in the Canton of Ticino separate treatment. For this reason, changes to BVG, KVG or withholding tax cannot be derived from the text.
For a separate payroll comparison, use the calcolatore stipendio.
